mainEntity.name: Why use Fiordland instead of CachyOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fiordland adds a tested stable channel built from Arch snapshots, system fixes that arrive with updates as one-time migrations, bootable Btrfs snapshots with one-command rollback, tawaki (one package manager for the Arch repos, Flathub and the AUR), its own installer and apps, and automatic tuning for low-end hardware.

mainEntity.name: Does Fiordland use the CachyOS kernel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fiordland 1 ships linux-fiord, its own fork of the CachyOS kernel packaging, built from the same CachyOS kernel source with the BORE scheduler, 1000 Hz timer, BBRv3 and x86-64 baseline builds so it runs on any 64-bit PC. The CachyOS kernel and the stock Arch kernel can still be chosen in the installer.

mainEntity.name: What does CachyOS do better than Fiordland?

acceptedAnswer.text: CachyOS rebuilds the Arch repositories for x86-64-v3 and v4 CPUs, enables ananicy-cpp with a large rules set, offers more kernel variants and has a longer track record. Fiordland 1 is the first release out of beta.
Yes. Fiordland Linux is free and open source, and every tool it ships is on GitHub.
